item.content: {"url": "https://api.crossref.org/works?query=architectural+requirements+for+artificial+intelligence+to+transition+from+episodic+memory+to+persistent+personal+identity&rows=4&select=DOI%2Ctitle%2Cabstract%2CURL%2Cpublished", "scope": "Crossref bibliographic metadata and abstracts where supplied; not full papers", "excerpt": "[{\"DOI\": \"10.2139/ssrn.6349019\", \"title\": [\"Persistent Memory Architectures for Personal Artificial Intelligence Systems\"], \"abstract\": \"<jats:p>Recent advances in large language models have significantly expanded the capabilities of conversational artificial intelligence systems. Transformer-based architectures enable models capable of reasoning, summarization, and natural language interaction across a wide range of domains. Despite these advances, most deployed systems remain fundamentally stateless. Interactions are typically constrained by bounded context windows and lack persistent understanding of individual users. This limitation restricts the development of truly personal artificial intelligence systems capable of long-term interaction, adaptation, and cognitive support. Human cognition develops across time through accumulated experiences and reflection. Artificial intelligence systems that cannot store and interpret long-term memory remain limited in their ability to support these processes. This paper proposes a conceptual framework for persistent memory in personal artificial intelligence systems. We introduce a layered memory architecture consisting of conversational memory, semantic memory, and reflective memory. These memory layers enable artificial intelligence systems to maintain evolving representations of individuals and support long-term interaction. Persistent memory architectures may therefore represent a foundational component of next-generation personal artificial intelligence systems designed to augment human reflection, decision-making, and cognitive processes.</jats:p>\", \"URL\": \"https://doi.org/10.2139/ssrn.6349019\", \"published\": {\"date-parts\": [[2026]]}}, {\"DOI\": \"10.7551/mitpress/10591.003.0005\", \"title\": [\"Situating Episodic Memory\"], \"URL\": \"https://doi.org/10.7551/mitpress/10591.003.0005\", \"published\": {\"date-parts\": [[2016, 2, 5]]}}, {\"DOI\": \"10.54941/ahfe1004643\", \"title\": [\"Episodic Memory with Interactive 3D Sequential Graph\"], \"abstract\": \"<jats:p>Episodic…
